title: Fidelity Balancer idea pad (per-request cost/quality dial)
content:
Quick brain dump on a feature tentatively called 'Fidelity Balancer' — a per-request/per-route control that lets apps programmatically trade latency/cost for generation fidelity (quality/creativity/length) without changing prompts or models.

Problem statement:
- Many customers want the same endpoint to serve a mix of high-fidelity and low-cost traffic (e.g., human-facing summaries vs. background analytics).
- Current levers (full model switch, quantization, static batching policies) are coarse and require separate deployments or manual routing rules.
- Ops complexity skyrockets when teams maintain multiple model endpoints for every fidelity tier.

High-level idea:
- Add a lightweight per-request policy parameter ("fidelity": numeric or enum) that the routing/runtime interprets into a sequence of actions: model variant selection, sampling/temperature overrides, max tokens cap, kv/cache reuse, early-stopping heuristics, and batching priority.
- Integrate with Console and SDKs so product teams can set route defaults, per-customer overrides, and A/B test fidelity bands.

User stories:
- As a product engineer, I want an endpoint that can accept a fidelity hint (0..100 or low/med/high) so I can reduce billable tokens for background jobs while keeping the chat UX high-quality.
- As a platform engineer, I want the runtime to map fidelity->model variant automatically (e.g., high -> 13B fp16, low -> 7B int4) while preserving latency SLOs.
- As an SRE, I want fidelity policies to influence queuing and batching priority so low-fidelity jobs can be deferred during peak with no impact on critical traffic.

Concrete mapping examples (initial thought):
- fidelity=high: model=redwood-13b-fp16, temp default=0.7, max_tokens=800, batch_priority=high, cache_ttl=short, run_eval_hook=on
- fidelity=medium: model=redwood-7b-fp16, temp=0.6, max_tokens=400, batch_priority=normal, cache_ttl=medium
- fidelity=low: model=redwood-4b-int4, temp=0.3, max_tokens=200, batch_priority=low, allow_prefix-trimming=true, early-stop-heuristic=enabled

Runtime considerations / constraints:
- Need a mapping layer in the control plane: fidelity policy -> candidate model set + runtime execution profile. Should be declarative and versioned.
- Kernel selection & quantization: ensure the selected model variants are actually compatible with fallback policies. Consider 'compatible-variants' metadata per model.
- Token accounting: low-fidelity often uses shorter max_tokens but may still consume prefix tokens. Consider auto-prefix-compression + prefix cache reuse.
- Batching interactions: lower fidelity requests should be grouped separately or flagged to allow elastic batching without impacting latency SLOs for high-fidelity.
- Monitoring: surface per-fidelity cost, latency, quality (via evals/LLM-metric hooks). Hook to Optimize recommendations.

API surface ideas:
- SDK: client.request({model: "redwood-infer", prompt, fidelity: "low"})
- REST: POST /v1/outputs {"model":"redwood-infer","input":"...","fidelity":"40"} // numeric 0-100
- Console: per-route fidelity default, per-customer overrides, quota multipliers by fidelity band

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Control-plane mapping exists for fidelity->(model, token caps, temp) for at least 3 bands.
- SDK and REST accept fidelity hint and server honors it.
- Metrics emitted: fidelity tag on traces, per-fidelity token counts, per-fidelity P50/P95 latencies, and per-fidelity cost estimate.
- Basic fallback: if chosen variant is unavailable, an automatic graceful fallback to nearest fidelity rather than 503.

Open questions / risks:
- How do we measure "quality" to validate fidelity bands? Need quick eval suites (small prompt sets) to estimate degradation curve. Tie to Optimize alerts.
- Billing model: do we bill by actual model used + tokens or a fidelity-weighted rate? Need finance input.
- Security/enterprise: some customers may require fidelity=high always; need per-account enforced minimums.
- UX: too many knobs are confusing. Consider simple enum + advanced tuning hidden behind Console.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Spike: implement prototype mapping in local dev cluster -> route fidelity hint through router to pick stored model alias (2-week spike). Owner: Marco.
- Quick eval: pick 50 prompts and measure quality drop for low/med/high across 3 model variants. Owner: Jia.
- Console mockups: per-route fidelity toggle + histogram view. Owner: Product design (ask Mei).
- Ops checklist: define metrics to create dashboards and alerting thresholds.

Notes to self (random):
- Could we reuse existing rollout framework so fidelity changes can be rolled out gradually? Maybe treat fidelity-band mappings as a deployable config.
- Think about session consistency: for chat session, fidelity stickiness matters. Option: fidelity_hint can be sticky per session ID unless overridden.
- Consider a "graceful degrade" mode where high-fidelity requests can be downgraded temporarily but marked as such on response header for client metrics.

Rough sketch of how router might evaluate a request:
1) parse fidelity hint (explicit > account default > route default)
2) consult fidelity-policy config for eligible variants (sorted by fidelity score)
3) check capacity for top variant; if capacity OK allocate, else try next variant, up to fallback threshold
4) attach chosen execution profile to request metadata (temp, max_tokens, batch_priority)
5) emit trace tag with chosen fidelity and fallback info

That's enough for now. Want to keep this as an informal parking lot while we validate with the OSS/runtime teams. Add any thinking or constraints you hit directly here so we don't forget.

-- lena
